Type: Feat, Fix, Refactor, Perf, Doc, Test, CI, or Chore.

Title: no letter-case restriction.
Reverts: use GitHub's default title, Revert "original title".
Examples: [Fix] attention: Fix KV cache indexing; [Perf] [AMD] flash-attn: Optimize decode performance. -->

## Motivation

On ROCm 10.1 with torch 2.12+, torch.profiler collects no GPU events.
### root cause
PyTorch 2.12 switched kineto to rocprofiler-sdk, which tracks its registered client in an environment variable; PyTorch 2.11 used roctracer and never reads that variable.
The sglang parent process initializes HIP, which sets `ROCPROFILER_REGISTER_LIBRARY` in its environment, and every child process inherits that value.
The child process then believes a profiler is already registered, so it never registers its own, and `torch.profiler` reports
no GPU activity at all, no kernels, no HIP API calls, and no error.

## Modifications

gated by ```_is_hip (torch_built_with_hip())```, AMD specific.

## Accuracy Tests

<!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. -->

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Both paths were tested on gfx1250, ROCm 10.1 / torch 2.12.

**Diffusion** — FLUX.2-dev 1024x1024, 6 steps:

```bash
SGLANG_DIFFUSION_PLATFORM_OVERRIDE=rocm ENABLE_CK=0 \
SGLANG_DIFFUSION_TORCH_PROFILER_DIR=$OUT \
sglang generate \
  --model-path $FLUX2_PATH \
  --prompt "A cinematic shot of a cute cat wearing a tiny astronaut helmet." \
  --num-gpus 1 --tp-size 1 --width 1024 --height 1024 \
  --num-inference-steps 6 --profile --num-profiled-timesteps 3
```

| trace category | before | after |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `kernel` | 0 | 5,331 |
| `cuda_runtime` | 0 | 9,533 |
| `ac2g` | 0 | 14,864 |
| `cpu_op` | 23,848 | 23,848 |

**LLM serving** — gpt-oss-120b-w-mxfp4-a-fp8, TP 1:

```bash
TRITON_HIP_USE_EXPERT_SCHEDULING=0 ENABLE_CK=0 \
SGLANG_TORCH_PROFILER_DIR=$OUT \
python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path amd/gpt-oss-120b-w-mxfp4-a-fp8 \
  --tp 1 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --max-running-requests 512 \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.9 \
  --attention-backend triton \
  --disable-radix-cache \
  --disable-cuda-graph \
  --port 8000

# with requests in flight, so there are forward steps to profile
python3 -m sglang.profiler --url http://127.0.0.1:8000 \
  --gpu --no-cpu --num-steps 5 --output-dir $OUT
```

| trace category | before | after |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `kernel` | 0 | 3,631 |
| `cuda_runtime` | 0 | 21,467 |
| `ac2g` | 0 | 25,098 |
| total events | 55 | 50,255 |

- [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).

- [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

`is_hip()` can't be used here. it lives in `srt/utils/common.py`, which does `import torch` at module scope, so importing it means importing torch. `import torch` is exactly when the inherited value gets read, so popping after that is a no-op. 
`environ._default_hip()` has the same problem, it resolves lazily after torch is in.

so i kept `_is_hip` gate but without importing torch via `torch_built_with_hip()` 

**2. moving them out of `environ.py`**

moved both to `python/sglang/srt/debug_utils/rocprofiler_register.py`


**3. env name**

renamed to `SGLANG_ROCM_KEEP_INHERITED_ROCPROFILER_REGISTER`.

@@ -0,0 +1,79 @@
+"""rocprofiler-register helpers.
+
+rocprofiler-register records the library that claimed registration in an
+environment variable, which exec then passes to every child. This module drops
+such an inherited claim. It runs before torch is imported, so nothing it
+imports may pull torch in.
+"""
+
+import importlib.util
+import os
+import pathlib
+
+from sglang.srt.environ import envs
+
+
+def torch_built_with_hip() -> bool:
+    """Whether torch is a ROCm build, without importing torch.
+
+    Same answer as srt.utils.common.is_hip, but that one imports torch and this
+    has to run before torch is imported. torch/version.py is nothing but a few
+    constant assignments, so reading only that file is enough.
+    """
+    torch_spec = importlib.util.find_spec("torch")
+    if torch_spec is None or torch_spec.origin is None:
+        return False
+    version_path = pathlib.Path(torch_spec.origin).with_name("version.py")
+    version_spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("torch_version", version_path)
+    if version_spec is None or version_spec.loader is None:
+        return False
+    version = importlib.util.module_from_spec(version_spec)
+    try:
+        version_spec.loader.exec_module(version)
+    except OSError:
+        return False
+    return getattr(version, "hip", None) is not None
+
+
+def _rocprofiler_sdk_already_loaded() -> bool:
+    """Check whether this process has already loaded a rocprofiler-sdk library.
+
+    A profiler that is really running has loaded its library into this process,
+    so the library shows up in the process memory map. If this function cannot
+    read that map, it returns True, and the caller then treats the process as
+    one where a profiler may be running and changes nothing.
+    """
+    try:
+        with open("/proc/self/maps") as f:
+            return "librocprofiler-sdk" in f.read()
+    except OSError:
+        return True
+
+
+def clear_inherited_rocprofiler_registration():
+    """Delete ROCPROFILER_REGISTER_LIBRARY if this process inherited it.
+
+    When a profiler registers, HIP writes the library path into the environment
+    variable ROCPROFILER_REGISTER_LIBRARY. A child process inherits that
+    variable, so the child thinks a profiler has already registered and refuses
+    to register its own. torch.profiler in the child then records CPU rows
+    only: it reports no GPU events and no error.
+
+    Only ROCm sets this variable, so this function returns right away on a CUDA
+    build. Only PyTorch 2.12 and newer hit the problem, because of
+    rocprofiler-sdk; PyTorch 2.11 and older use roctracer, so deleting the
+    variable changes nothing for them.
+
+    This function deletes the variable only when no profiler is running in this
+    process, so it never breaks a profiler that is really collecting data.
+    The process must call this function before it imports torch.
+    """
+    if os.environ.get("ROCPROFILER_REGISTER_LIBRARY") is None:
+        return
+    if not torch_built_with_hip():
+        return
+    if envs.SGLANG_ROCM_KEEP_INHERITED_ROCPROFILER_REGISTER.get():
+        return
+    if _rocprofiler_sdk_already_loaded():
+        return
+    os.environ.pop("ROCPROFILER_REGISTER_LIBRARY", None)
